common_name: Easter Bonnet Deep Pink Sweet Alyssum (Compact Early-Blooming Rose-Pink Selection)

planting.note: Surface-sow a few weeks before the last frost, since the fine seed needs light to germinate; this individual color selection from the Easter Bonnet series blooms earlier and holds its compact habit longer than older mixed strains.

directions: Scatter seed onto firmed, well-drained soil and press it in without covering, since alyssum seed germinates best with light exposure. This uniform, rose-pink selection from the Easter Bonnet series holds a tidy, dense mound through the cool season and is prized for earlier flowering than older alyssum types. Use it as edging or filler in mixed containers where its honey scent can be enjoyed up close, and shear the planting back lightly once flowering slows in warm weather to push out a fresh round of bloom.

common_name: Easter Bonnet Lavender Sweet Alyssum (Compact Early-Blooming Lavender Selection)

planting.note: Surface-sow a few weeks before the last frost into well-drained soil; the fine seed needs light and should not be covered.

directions: Direct sow onto the soil surface without covering, since light aids germination of this fine seed. Easter Bonnet Lavender forms a neat, low mound of soft lavender flowers with the classic sweet honey fragrance, staying compact and tidy longer into the season than heirloom alyssum strains. It is well suited to edging, rock gardens, and window boxes where its scent carries at close range, and it benefits from a light shearing mid-season if bloom slows during a summer heat spell.

common_name: Easter Bonnet Violet Sweet Alyssum (Compact Early-Blooming Deep Purple Selection)

planting.note: Surface-sow a few weeks before the last frost; do not cover the seed, as it germinates best with light exposure.

directions: Press seed onto firmed soil without burying it, since it needs light to sprout reliably. This deep-purple selection from the Easter Bonnet series packs an especially rich, saturated color into the same tidy, mounding habit that makes the series useful for edging and container work. It flowers earlier in spring than older seed strains and tolerates brief warm spells better, though a mid-summer shearing will renew bloom if flowering fades in peak heat.

common_name: Easter Bonnet White Sweet Alyssum (Compact Early-Blooming Pure White Selection)

planting.note: Surface-sow a few weeks before the last frost; the tiny seed needs light and should be left uncovered.

directions: Sow onto the soil surface and press in gently without covering, since light triggers germination. Easter Bonnet White covers itself in pure white flowers with a small green eye, forming a dense, uniform mound that reads as a clean edging ribbon along beds and walkways. It shares the series' earlier bloom time and improved heat tolerance compared to older white alyssum strains, and a light shearing after the first big flush keeps plants tidy and reblooming through the season.

common_name: Clear Crystal Purple Shades Sweet Alyssum (Tetraploid Large-Flowered Purple Alyssum)

planting.note: Surface-sow around the last frost in evenly moist, well-drained soil; this tetraploid selection has noticeably larger flowers and stems than standard diploid alyssum and appreciates more consistent watering.

directions: Press the seed onto firmed, evenly moist soil without covering, as germination depends on light. Clear Crystal Purple Shades is a tetraploid sweet alyssum bred for oversized, richly fragrant lavender-purple florets and a more vigorous, heat-tolerant constitution than standard fine-textured alyssum. Keep the soil from drying out fully between waterings, especially in containers, since the larger foliage mass draws more moisture than older varieties. It performs well through a longer stretch of the growing season and rewards a mid-season trim if flowering slows during the hottest weeks.
sources: Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden Plant Trials

common_name: Clear Crystal Lavender Shades Sweet Alyssum (Tetraploid Large-Flowered Lavender Alyssum)

planting.note: Surface-sow around the last frost; keep soil evenly moist while seedlings establish, since this tetraploid strain is more vigorous and thirstier than standard alyssum.

directions: Sow onto the soil surface and press in without burying, since light is needed to trigger germination. Clear Crystal Lavender Shades produces soft lavender, white-tinged florets with a purple eye that are noticeably larger than typical alyssum blooms, a hallmark of its tetraploid breeding. It fills out into a fuller, more mounded plant than fine-textured heirloom alyssum and holds up better in heat and humidity, making it a strong choice for containers as well as beds. Water regularly to keep the root zone from drying, and shear lightly if flowering pauses during peak summer.

common_name: Clear Crystal White Sweet Alyssum (Tetraploid Large-Flowered White Alyssum)

planting.note: Surface-sow around the last frost; this tetraploid white companion to the Clear Crystal Purple and Lavender Shades needs consistent moisture and will not tolerate standing water.

directions: Press seed onto firmed, moist soil and leave uncovered, since alyssum germinates best in light. Clear Crystal White is the white-flowered anchor of the tetraploid Clear Crystal series, producing masses of oversized, sparkling white florets on a denser and more vigorous plant than older fine-flowered alyssum. It creates an airy, cloud-like drift along path edges and container rims and continues blooming further into summer than heirloom strains, provided the soil is kept evenly moist and never allowed to become waterlogged. Trim lightly if the planting becomes sparse in the height of summer to renew flowering.

common_name: Wonderland White Sweet Alyssum (Fleuroselect Gold Medal Dwarf White Alyssum)

planting.note: Surface-sow around the last frost into well-drained soil; Wonderland White is a Fleuroselect Gold Medal-winning selection valued for its dense, semi-trailing habit in both beds and containers.

directions: Scatter seed onto the soil surface without covering, since germination is light-dependent. Wonderland White forms a rounded, semi-trailing dwarf mound smothered in fragrant white flowers, making it equally at home spilling over a container edge or filling a garden border. Its vigorous spread and strong garden performance earned it a Fleuroselect Gold Medal, and it holds its floral display well into summer with regular watering. Shear the mound back lightly if growth becomes leggy to encourage dense rebloom.

common_name: Wonderland Deep Purple Sweet Alyssum (Fleuroselect Gold Medal Dwarf Purple Alyssum)

planting.note: Surface-sow around the last frost; do not cover the seed, since light improves germination of this vigorous, dwarf, semi-trailing selection.

directions: Press seed onto firmed soil and leave it uncovered so light can trigger germination. Wonderland Deep Purple carries intensely saturated purple flowers over a tight, rounded, semi-trailing mound, giving strong color impact in small containers or as a border edge. Like the rest of the award-winning Wonderland series, it spreads vigorously for its compact size and keeps flowering through summer with consistent moisture. A light shearing after the first heavy bloom flush keeps the color dense and the habit tidy.

common_name: Wonderland Deep Rose Sweet Alyssum (Compact Dwarf Rose-Pink Alyssum)

planting.note: Surface-sow around the last frost into well-drained soil; leave seed uncovered, as it germinates best with light exposure.

directions: Sow onto the soil surface without covering, since alyssum seed needs light to germinate reliably. Wonderland Deep Rose smothers its low, dense mound in clusters of fragrant rose-pink flowers that stand out among the more common white and purple alyssum shades. Its foliage stays low and tight to the ground while the plant spreads outward vigorously, making it a good filler between taller bedding plants or a color accent in mixed containers. Keep soil consistently moist and shear back after the first bloom flush to prompt a fresh round of color.

common_name: Purple Stream Sweet Alyssum (Vegetative Heat-Tolerant Trailing Purple Alyssum)

planting.note: Set out rooted transplants at or shortly after the last frost; Purple Stream is a vegetatively propagated, Danziger-bred selection sold only as plugs or liners, not seed, and bred specifically for heat tolerance through summer.

directions: Plant rooted transplants after the last frost into well-drained soil or a container mix, since this cultivar is propagated only vegetatively and is not available as seed. Purple Stream carries dark purple, sun-fast flowers on a dense, semi-trailing plant bred to keep blooming through summer heat that stalls standard seed-grown alyssum. Its cascading habit makes it a strong choice for hanging baskets and mixed container rims, and it benefits from steady moisture rather than the drier conditions tolerated by older heirloom alyssum. No deadheading is required, as spent flowers drop cleanly on their own.

common_name: White Stream Sweet Alyssum (Vegetative Heat-Tolerant Trailing White Alyssum)

planting.note: Set out rooted transplants at or shortly after the last frost; White Stream is a vegetatively propagated selection sold as plugs or liners rather than seed, bred for continued bloom through summer heat.

directions: Set transplants into well-drained garden soil or containers after the last frost, since White Stream is only available as a vegetatively propagated plug, not as seed. It produces a dense, vigorous, semi-trailing mound of fragrant white flowers that keeps blooming through summer conditions that cause seed-grown alyssum to fade, making it a dependable choice for hanging baskets and mixed containers. Water regularly to support its heavier growth habit, and let spent flowers drop on their own since deadheading is not needed to maintain continuous bloom.

common_name: Lavender Stream Sweet Alyssum (Vegetative Heat-Tolerant Trailing Lavender Alyssum)

planting.note: Set out rooted transplants at or shortly after the last frost; Lavender Stream rounds out the Stream series and, like its purple and white counterparts, is propagated only vegetatively.

directions: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants into well-drained soil or containers after the last frost, since Lavender Stream is not sold as seed. It produces soft lavender flowers over the same dense, semi-trailing, heat-tolerant habit that defines the Stream series, allowing it to keep blooming through summer stretches that stop older seed-grown alyssum. Its cascading growth makes it useful for softening container rims and hanging baskets alongside its purple and white series-mates, and steady watering keeps the mound full and floriferous through the season.

common_name: Blushing Princess Sweet Alyssum (Vegetative Color-Changing White-to-Lavender Alyssum)

planting.note: Plant transplants at or shortly after the last frost; Blushing Princess is a patented, vegetatively propagated sweet alyssum sold as plugs, not seed, and is a heavier water user than most alyssum.

directions: Set out rooted transplants after the last frost into fertile, well-drained soil or a container mix, since this patented cultivar is propagated only vegetatively. Blushing Princess opens fresh white flowers that gradually blush to soft lavender-pink as they age, giving the mat-forming, trailing plant a two-toned, sparkling look at any given moment. It is a heavier water user than most alyssum and should not be allowed to dry out between waterings, and its vigorous growth pairs best with equally vigorous companions in mixed plantings. No deadheading is needed to sustain the long, continuous bloom.

common_name: Frosty Knight Sweet Alyssum (Sterile Variegated Heat-Tolerant Lobularia Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant transplants at or after the last frost; Frosty Knight is a sterile, vegetatively propagated interspecific hybrid (L. maritima x L. canariensis) sold only as plugs, bred for much greater heat tolerance than seed-grown alyssum.

directions: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after the last frost, since this sterile hybrid produces no viable seed and is not available in seed form. Frosty Knight combines fragrant white flowers with pale chartreuse-edged foliage, giving it visual interest even between bloom flushes, and its interspecific parentage grants it markedly better heat tolerance than standard sweet alyssum. Because it never sets seed, energy goes entirely into continuous flowering and trailing growth rather than seed production, so it needs no deadheading. Give it afternoon shade in hot climates and consistent moisture to keep the dense, spilling mound at its best through summer.

common_name: Snowdrift Sweet Alyssum (Classic AGM Tetraploid Pure White Alyssum)

planting.note: Surface-sow around the last frost into light, moderately fertile, well-drained soil; Snowdrift is a long-established tetraploid strain and holder of the RHS Award of Garden Merit.

directions: Press the tiny seed onto firmed soil without covering, since light is needed for reliable germination. Snowdrift is a classic tetraploid sweet alyssum that forms low mounds of fresh green foliage covered almost completely in brilliant white, intensely fragrant flowers from early summer into fall. It has held the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for its dependable garden performance, and its compact, uniform habit suits formal edging as well as gaps in paving and rock gardens. Shear plants back by about a third if bloom slows during hot spells to renew flowering as conditions cool.
